meaning: to work or study late into the night
example: She burned the midnight oil to finish her essay before the deadline.
origin: Comes from the time when people worked and studied by the light of oil lamps late at night

wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with wasting oil; it describes working or studying late.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to cook a meal very late at night
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The words suggest cooking, but the idiom is about working or studying hard at night.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to sleep deeply through the whole night
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which describes staying awake to work or study.

explanation: 'Burn the midnight oil' means to stay up late to work or study. Learners may take the words literally, so it helps to focus on the idea of spending late hours on effort.
